text:
maria: heads up — saw a sustained p95 latency bump (~2x) in the dedicated-gpu pool during a recent scale-up around 18:12 UTC. traces point to ~700-900ms of extra time in the first few tokens for new allocs.
kevin: confirming, I pulled the node-level metrics. NVMe io_wait jumps during warm pool fills. also image pulls spiking. suspect KV cache materialization + image pulls competing for IO.
oliver: fwiw i saw a bunch of kernel compile logs at the same time. when a model variant routes to a node with no precompiled kernels we compile on first inference — adds ~200-400ms. logs:```
[2026-02-05T18:12:24Z] kernel_compiler: compiling kernel set for llama-compat (seq=2048) 
[2026-02-05T18:12:24Z] kernel_compiler: compiled 12 kernels in 312ms
```
chloe: interesting. so multiple sources: kernel compile, kv cache write/read, and image pulls. do we have a breakdown of where the extra 700-900ms goes?
maria: rough breakdown from traces: kernel compile ~250ms, KV materialize (read+deserialize) ~300ms, image pull / container start + network ~150ms. small remainder in scheduler queuing.
kevin: sharing iostat snippet from affected host:```
Device:         tps    kB_read/s    kB_wrtn/s    await
nvme0n1        112.4       10.2        720.5      35.4
```
kevin: write throughput is huge due to KV prefetch dumping many small files to local disk and then reading them back. NVMe queue depth spiking.
chloe: do we write the KV cache as many small files? can we switch to a single mmap'd blob or use tmpfs during warmup?
kevin: currently we materialize per-shard files under /var/lib/kv_cache/<model>/<shard>. that creates many small writes. tmpfs could help but memory pressure on gpu hosts is tight.
oliver: alternative — stream-deserialize on first read (lazy) instead of materializing everything. tradeoff is per-request CPU hit but avoids IO storm during scale-up.
maria: another complication: autoscaler tries to fill warm pool immediately after capacity event. we get 8 nodes coming up concurrently => concurrent KV materialize + kernel compile across all. noisy neighbor IO.
kevin: also saw cloud registry 429s when many nodes pulled the container at once. image pull retries add 50-200ms per host. we can reduce by pre-pulling images on warm pool nodes or use a local pull-through cache.
sre-bot: incident created — INC-2026-1087 "autoscale init latency: kv/io/compile storm". paging on-call.
chloe: quick mitigations I propose: 1) stagger warm-pool fill by adding jitter to autoscaler start times, 2) reduce concurrent prefetch threads per host (to limit io concurrency), 3) prefer precompiled kernels for common shapes (fast path).
kevin: +1. also add a guard: if nvme await > X ms, backoff materialization and fallback to lazy load. quick patch I can push.
maria: for immediate rollback: reduced warm pool fill rate at 18:23 and observed p95 back to normal within 4 minutes. deploy-bot: canary rolled back three canaries automatically due to latency threshold.
deploy-bot: rollback triggered by latency-alerts (rule: any model route p95 > 1.5x baseline for 3m).
oliver: longer-term: build an artifact store for precompiled kernels and add a startup hook that warms kernel cache before serving. also consider packing KV shards into a single LZ4 blob to reduce files+syscalls.
kevin: notes & TODOs: 
- implement IO backoff guard (kevin)
- add jitter to warm pool fill (maria + autoscaler)
- evaluate tmpfs vs blob format for KV (oliver + kevin)
- prepull images or enable registry cache (infra)
- add metric for kernel_compile_time and kv_materialize_time (chloe)
maria: filing a follow-up RFC for warm-pool startup heuristics + precompile strategy. tagging @oncall for visibility. :thumbsup:
chloe: agreed. i'll add charts to dashboard and create alerts for nvme await and concurrent prefetch count.
maria: thanks all — good triage. will update INC-2026-1087 with investigation notes and immediate mitigations.
